metadata.title: What Trump's clamp down on Anthropic is signaling to rest of the world

content.text:
The Trump administration pushes harder on Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) after the private AI developer pulled its Claude Mythos and Fable 5 models from the market in response to demands to cut AI product access to foreign governments.
Yahoo Finance Tech Editor Dan Howley joins the Market Domination team in reporting on the day's biggest tech headlines.
Bloomberg has a new story. Trump's Anthropic crackdown sets off alarms for US allies. Basically talking about how the administration told Anthropic, listen, you're going to block foreign nationals from accessing the newest AI models. Our allies upset? What do you make about it?
I think it's it's interesting to see how this is just one reaction to from from one company's model. Now, the big thing about this was that uh it's it's their Fable 5 model. It's based on their Mythos class models, their Claude Mythos, they had a Claude Mythos preview. They said, hey, look, this thing is good at uh hacking or or finding flaws in software that can then be exploited. kind of call hacking.
Uh and so, uh they released it as part of this Project Glasswing to, you know, Apple, Microsoft, uh Amazon, all these companies, so that they can use it to then find flaws and uh remediate them in their software to prevent them from being hacked in the future. Uh and so then they, you know, kind of held off on releasing it publicly. Fable 5 is a version that's publicly, or was publicly available, uh that was supposed to be able to offer the capabilities of a Mythos class without
being used for say, making a pipe bomb or something. It would go ahead and revert back to Opus 4.8, it's next powerful model, uh when you try to ask it questions along those lines. Uh and that was kind of the the go-to. And now the administration's saying that they found a flaw. Uh Anthropic basically saying it's not really actually that big of a deal. You can find this with, you know, GPT 5.5 or or anything along those lines. Um but I think I think the the kind of
takeaway from this is going to be a larger kind of scattering of the AI market, right? Because if you think about it, you're you're in the UK, you're in France, you're in, you know, uh uh Japan. Uh it's, you know, it's not just foreign nationals that are uh adversaries, it's allies as well. It's it's anybody that's
Well, I want to I want to do you think something like this, does it ultimately end up helping European AI companies to the extent that European governments now say, you know what, you know what, we really need our own AI tools and alternatives here.
I do. I think that that's that's what will happen. We have Mistral, obviously, uh in France. Uh, you know, and they are doing relatively well. I think that that capability will just continue to spread throughout the rest of the world where or or or or need rather, because they're going to say, okay, well we can't get access to the best of the best from the US. So I guess we have to make the best of the best now. And so we could see this kind of unfold as kind of a back and forth drama. Now,
you know, what does that mean for Anthropic? They're obviously going to continue to try to fight this, get those models back online. It's a big deal because customers don't then get access to it. It's not as though this has been out for quite some time. It's just last week. But, you know, customers want access to the best models out there and right now they can't get access to Anthropic's best model. I think it's it's it's going to be something that unless this is sorted out quickly, could become, as you said, a bigger problem for US companies because now they're going to start getting more competition from elsewhere.
